discovery: Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution (BB84 and entanglement-based E91)

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

nominees.name: Artur K. Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84, 1984) showed that the quantum principles of measurement disturbance and no-cloning allow two parties to establish a secret key whose security is guaranteed by physical law rather than computational assumptions. Ekert (1991) independently linked key distribution to entanglement, making violation of Bell inequalities a direct certificate of security and founding the path to device-independent cryptography. These works turned quantum foundations into a physical resource: the first realisation of quantum information science as a technology. They launched decades of photon-counting, single-photon and entanglement experiments worldwide, culminating in fibre and satellite QKD networks spanning thousands of kilometres. The 2022 Prize recognised experimental tests of entanglement; the conceptual discovery that quantum physics enables provably secure communication remains unrecognised and has transformed both physics and society.
